# The Unmooring
[textlink="The Collapse" link="WFLoreCollapse"] did not leave an ordinary black hole. Kyphrus is wrong. Light bends the wrong way around it, clocks near it disagree, and the further a ship flies from the sector's heart, the less reality agrees with itself. Spacers call it [color=#d070ff]the Unmooring[/color].
The only reason the inner sector is livable is [textlink="the Lattice" link="WFLoreLattice"]: six anchors that hold reality in place around Caelestinus Central.
## The bands
Where the Lattice is strong, space is [bold]Moored[/bold]. Past about 18 kilometres from the centre its hold weakens, and every navigation computer marks the border as restricted, unsafe space.
- [color=#e0b040]Slack[/color]: the hold is thin. Instruments stutter and crews hear things. - [color=#e08030]Adrift[/color]: the hold barely reaches. Ships answer hails nobody sent. - [color=#e04030]Untethered[/color]: the Lattice does not reach. Turn back. - [color=#d030a0]the Deep[/color]: past 30 kilometres. Its name never comes out of a console the same way twice.
The bands follow the anchors, not the map. When an anchor falls, the bands slide inward on its side.
## Drift
The longer a ship stays out, the more it [bold]Drifts[/bold]. Drift builds slowly in the Slack, fast in the Untethered, and without limit in the Deep. It fades again once a ship comes home.
A crew deep in Drift sees and hears what is not there: footsteps in an empty corridor, a contact on the scope that vanishes, a voice on the common channel that knows their names, a figure at the end of the hall that is gone when they reach it. Nobody else aboard sees the same thing. The screen swims. Instruments lie.
In the Deep the Unmooring stops pretending. The smallest minds aboard go first: a ship's cat or a mouse in the vents goes still, then gets back up as one of the [textlink="Remade" link="WFLoreMonolith"].
## Why anyone goes
Because the far bands are rich. The asteroids out there carry more ore the further they lie from the anchors, and past the Adrift line the rock holds [color=#d070ff]exotic matter[/color]: shards of something that should not hold together, worth a fortune at any buyer and the only thing that can build a new anchor.
Crews who go deep carry a [bold]Drift stabiliser[/bold], a small anchor of their own that keeps a little moored space around the ship, and an [bold]anchor charm[/bold] round the neck for when they have to step outside.
Some who go deep do not want to come back. See [textlink="the Choir" link="WFLoreChoir"].
